Name: Forage of Ferngill
Author: StunkyMcDoo123
Description:
Thank you to those who reached out to me over the last few months. I have been having a lot of troubles with my mental health this year, which has now caused me to lose my job. I am doing better with Medication and Therapy, but am a long way from being able to return to modding.

I am looking for someone who wishes to take caretaker over my mods while I deal with personal issues. It can be a simple maintenance ownership to ensure it works with updates and gets bugs fixed, implement what I could not or expand with their own vision.

If you are interested in this, please drop me a message here or on Discord (stunkymcdoo) and we can have a chat about what I had planned, I can provide any in dev bits and bobs and chat about what you would like to do. 

******************************************************************************************************************************************************************

Welcome Foragers of Ferngill!!

I really enjoyed the Foraging aspect of the game, but felt there just wasn't a lot to find. So, I decided to create Forage of Ferngill. This mod adds dozens of new forageable Mushrooms, Flowers Fruits and more to the Valley all throughout the year. Some are common, some are rare and some can only bound found in very specific places so you will have to search high and low to find them all!

[center][b][size=3]*** FOF -- A series of Foraging Mods ***[/size][/b]
I'll be honest with you all, I've not been too happy with this mod for a while. When I released it I was pretty much the only new foraging goods game in town. Most forage mods just let you forage existing things that couldnt be foraged, or only added one or two items pretty much everywhere. I created FOF to fill the gap I saw in my world; A mod that added brand new things to forage that were integrated into the world in a way that made sense. I was happy for a while. Since then, Modders like Wildflour or the Cornucopia team have produced some excellent mods, to the point where I don't feel I even get a consideration anymore when people are making mod lists, or recommending mods. I am partly to blame for this as I am not an active member of the Discord or other message boards, but I'm not a very outgoing person anyway. This was a little bit heart-breaking at first, but I have forced myself to remember why I made FOF in the first place. So, going forward I am re-growing Forage of Ferngill into something else. Forage of Ferngill as it is has been "retired". The merged file will still be available for anyone who wants to use it, but I am reconsidering everything in the mod and re-growing eveything. Some things may not be part of my new vision for the mod, we will see.

The first of the regrowths will be "Much Ado About Mushrooms". The mushrooms part is what I started with, and what I like the most about this mod. I've done my best to produce some nice images to explain what 'MAAM' is about below. I'm no good with Photoshop and whatnot so these are pretty basic. I've also updated the changelog with a more detailed selection of changes.

Also honestly, and easier to admit to people I don't know, I've had a work stress related breakdown. The version uploaded isn't finished as I wanted to get Mt Vapius and East Scarp forage and gift tastes in, and add some recipe amendments for Wildflour Forager, but getting this released 'as is' is a step to getting things out of my head and into an area I can control. 

Thank you to everyone who has used both Forage of Ferngill and Grapes of Ferngill. I hope to continue working on them going forward

[b]*** A CAVALCADE OF KOMBUCHA ***[/b]
A Cavalcade of Kombucha is a complete re-brewing of the Kombucha section of Forage of Ferngill. The mod has been completely converted over to Content Patcher, so PFM is no longer needed. It does need Extra Machine Configs though. There has been some artwork tweaks and production tweaks, the biggest of which is Wild Leaf has been removed and you use Tea Leaves instead. There is baked in compatibility for those using Realistic Shop Inventories, and should be compatible with mod added items for making Kombucha. As before, it is not compatible with the old FOF Kombucha module, so if updating you will need to sell all your Kombucha, Scoby and remove your Scoby Starters and Komucha Jars before doing so. New games of games that haven't used FOF Kobucha before this can be added with no issues.

ACOK offer the following to the budding Forager
Scoby Starter -- Learned at level 2 Foraging
Kombucha Jar -- Learned at level 4 Foraging
Scoby -- Produced every couple of days by the Scoby Stater. MUST be indoors
Plain Kombucha -- Tea Leaves + Scoby in the Kombucha Jar
Sweet Kombucha -- Fruit + Plain Kombucha in the Kombucha Jar
Savoury Kombucha -- Vegetables or Forage + Plain Kombucha in the Kombucha Jar
Floral Kombucha -- Flowers + Plain Kombucha in the Kombucha Jar
Salty Kombucha -- Seaweed or Algae + Plain Kombucha in the Kombucha Jar
Umami Kombucha -- Mushrooms + Plain Kombucha in the Kombucha Jar
Nutty Kombucha -- Nuts or Seeds + Plain Kombucha in the Kombucha Jar

[b]*** FROM SOURCE TO SEA ***[/b]
From Source to Sea is a complete re-write of the Coastal section of Forage of Ferngill. I had a bit of inspiration return so completed this to use in my own new game. As it seems to work nicely I thought I would release it. No fancy pictures for this one I'm afraid. Here is what would be written on them though. This does not mean I am back. I have been contacted by a couple of people about looking after/taking over these mods and I am confident they will do well.

FSTS offer the following to the budding Forager
-- 3 new types of Coral --
-- 2 new seaonal Seashells --
-- 2 new types of Seaweed --
-- 2 new edible Seafoods (both can be bred in Fish Ponds) --
-- 3 new edible Aquatic plants --
-- 8 new dishes based around aquatic ingredients --
-- 1 new Magical Potion --
-- Inter-mod integration with Stardew Valley Expanded, Ridgeside Village, East Scarp, and Cornucopia --

FSTS introduces a number of new aquatic plant foragables to the valley. Anisea-weed and Spysea-weed can be found occasionally washing up on shore after rain, while Aquamint and Blue Algae can be found in and around rivers and lakes.

In addition the the plant based foragables, there are some Sealife based forageables to be found. Horn and Glasseye shells was up on beaches, and Ferngill Scallops can be found and caught in crab pots. There are tales spreading of a black deep sea urchin occasionally washing up after storms too. If only we could get to the sea floor...

Along with the new foragables, FSTS brings 8 new cooking recipes for you to enjoy. Gus sells a particular recipe every other Friday at the Saloon, starting on the 5th. The recipes are expanded if you have Cornucopia installed. 

You can also find three new types of Coral on Ginger Island. These can be combined to create a Coral Necklace, a wonderful charm that can be gifted as a universal like, or sold for a decent amount of gold.

[b]**MUSHROOMS OF FERNGILL**[/b]
[img]https://i.ibb.co/WgmjZPc/MUSHROOMS-OF-FERNGILL.png[/img]

Details on where to find the new Mushrooms

[SPOILER]-- White Mushrooms are the most common type of mushroom to be found in a supermarket. They are often fried with Garlic to create Garlic Mushrooms and can be found growing all over the valley in Spring.

The following Mushrooms only grow after Rain or Storms.

-- Dew Cup Mushroom are cream coloured bowl mushrooms that gather the morning dew into little puddles. They are usually baked with cheese into a Mushroom Tart and can be found growing in the Backwoods in Spring.

-- Muffin Bell Mushroom are orange bell shaped mushrooms that smell like fresh baked bread. They are a vital ingredient in Mushroom Soup and can be found growing at the Railway in Fall. 

-- Stalk Cluster Mushroom are thin stringy mushrooms that can be peeled apart. They are a vital ingredient in Mushroom Soup and can be found growing in the Mountains in Fall. 

-- Plump Belly Mushroom are fat stubby mushrooms with a deep rich flavour. They are a vital ingredient in Mushroom Soup and can be found growing  in the Forest in Fall. 

-- Yellow Mushroom is an oddly shaped umbrella mushroom that has a sweet smell. It is very poisonous so definitely don't eat it. They can be found growing On Ginger Island

-- Black Mushroom is a spindly peaked mushroom that is sticky to the touch. It is very poisonous so definitely don't eat it. They can be found growing in the Witches Swamp

-- Woodland Stool Mushroom are flat topped spotted mushrooms often used as resting spots by small woodland Animals. They are traditionally used to create Stuffed Mushroom as they are wide and deep enough to be filled. They can be found growing in Cindersap Forest and Stardew Valley Exapandeds Forest West 

-- Ridge Puff Mushroom are brown puffy mushrooms that grow high up on ridges. They are often used to make Fire-Spiced mushrooms as they have a natural kick to them. They can be found growing in the Mountain and in areas of Ridgeside Village.
-
- Tooting Horn Mushroom are long horn shaped mushrooms that whistle in the wind. They are often used to make Mushroom Tagliatelle as they have a delicate flavour. They can be found growing in Town and around East Scarp 

-- Spring Cap Mushroom are flat burgundy mushrooms that have a natural bounce to them. They are commonly used to create Mushroom and Ale pie as they have a rich flavour. They can be found growing in Cindersap Forest and along Cape Stardew 

-- Plump Belly, Dew Cup, Stalk Cluster and Muffin Bell mushrooms can be found in certain parts of Mt Vapius after Rain or Storms. Expert Mycologists suspect a unique mushroom may be found there but haven't identified one yet. Keep checking back though.[/SPOILER]
-- On Mondays Gus will sell a random recipe using the new Mushrooms.

-- At level 5 Combat you will figure out how to make the Witches Elixir. This powerful potion makes you tougher, stronger and faster but takes a heavy toll on your fatigue.

-- If you let Demetrius build some Mushroom boxes in your Cave, you will find the new mushrooms will grow there too!

[b]**ROOTS OF FERNGILL**[/b]
The second module of Forage of Ferngill is Roots of Ferngill. These edible roots can be found growing around the valley, but you'll have to dig them up first! They only grow in certain areas of the map and at certain times of year, so you'll have to look hard. The new roots are...
[img]https://i.ibb.co/RDg45TD/01-Roots.png[/img]
-- Gaelic-Root. This pungent root is a relative of Garlic but has a much sharper taste. It is often turned into a spread and added to either Bread or atop Halibut. They can be found growing [SPOILER] At the Bus Stop in Spring[/SPOILER]
-- Bardic-Root. This slightly bitter root has been know to have minor healing properties. It is often mixed with Dandelion to create a sharp beverage, or fried with Cave Carrot to make spicy Kinpara Gobo. They can be found growing [SPOILER] Near Robins house in Fall [/SPOILER]
-- Sabi-Root. This very spicy root is almost inedible by itself. It is usually crushed into a spicy green paste and added to Nigiri or Temaki. They can be found growing [SPOILER] Around the pond in the Forest in Summer [/SPOILER]

-- On Tuesdays Gus will sell a random recipe using the new Roots.
[img]https://i.ibb.co/qJJqvDt/02-Recipes.png[/img]﻿
-- Root Beer can be made by combining Hops with one of four different edible roots. These are show in the screenshots, but the list of roots you can use are [SPOILER] Gaelic Root, Bardic Root, Winter Root, Taro Root and Cave Carrot [/SPOILER]

-- Certain Roots can be fed into the Seed Maker to create growable versions. These are show in the screenshots, but the list of roots you can use are [SPOILER] Gaelic-Root, Bardic-Root, Sabi-Root and Spring Onion [/SPOILER]

Roots of Ferngill also supports some expansion mods. If you use Stardew Valley Expanded, Ridgeside VIllage, East Scarp, Cape Stardew and Mt Vapius you can find the Roots growing in some of their areas.


[b]**COASTAL FORAGE OF FERNGILL**[/b]
The third module of Forage of Ferngill is Coastal Forage of Ferngill. New things have started washing up on the beaches of Stardew Valley for you to collect.
[img]https://i.ibb.co/1nBDQyN/05-Seaweeds.png[/img]
[img]https://i.ibb.co/YLHrnG3/03-Seafood.png[/img]
-- Ferngill Scallops. This shellfish has a thick meaty flesh that is often fried up and served in the shell or on a platter. They can be found [SPOILER] At the Beach all year[/SPOILER]
-- Anisea-Weed. This deep black seaweed tastes like salty Liquorice and is often boiled down to make Laverbread. It can be found  [SPOILER] At the Beach all year; Also found at East Scarp and Cape Stardews beaches[/SPOILER] 
-- Spysea-Weed. This bright red seaweed have a spicy flavour and is often used to add a milder spice to Tomato sauces. It can be found [SPOILER] At the Beach all year; Also found at East Scarp and Cape Stardews beaches[/SPOILER] 

-- Glass-Eye Shell. This pick iridescent shell was once used as a glass eye by sailors of old.  It can be found [SPOILER] At the Beach in Spring[/SPOILER] 
-- Horn Shell. This spiky horn shaped shell echoes with the call of the sea.  It can be found [SPOILER] At the Beach in Fall[/SPOILER] 
[img]https://i.ibb.co/nmCMc76/02-Shells.png[/img]
-- There are a number of brightly coloured Corals that have started to wash up. While this may be a sign of damage to the local coral reef by increased fishing, Sailors have started making necklaces out of the pieces they have foraged as mementos of what the ocean means to them. Some people adore this type of necklace.
[img]https://i.ibb.co/rpRc0sb/01-Corals.png[/img]
-- On Fridays Gus will sell a random recipe using the new Seafoods.
[img]https://i.ibb.co/zZJKzMb/04-Seafood-Dishes.png[/img]
[b]

**FRUIT AND NUTS OF FERNGILL**
[/b]The fourth module of Forage and Ferngill bring new Fruit and Nuts to the valley and beyond. There are a number of sweet new berries growing on bushes or trees for you to find.
[img]https://i.ibb.co/HDYCTWF/01-Fruits.png[/img]
[img]https://i.ibb.co/LpZ15ZK/02-Nuts.png[/img]

-- Sol-Berry. These sweet pink berries grow in flatter clear areas of the Valley and are usually mixed with Cherries to create a delicious Sol Berry & Cherry Tart. They can be found growing at [SPOILER]The BusStop and Town during the last few days of Winter and the first few days of Spring [/SPOILER]
-- Nimbus-Berry. These pale berries are found growing higher in the valley and can be baked into a Nimbus-Berry Crostata. They can be found growing at [SPOILER]The Mountain, The Backwoods and The Railway during the last few days of Spring and the first few days of Summer [/SPOILER]
-- Bramble-berry. These small blue berries are grow in denser forested areas of the Valley and are popular baked into Bramble-Berry Muffins. They can be found growing at [SPOILER]The Forest and Woods during the last few days of Summer and the first few days of Fall [/SPOILER]
-- Crackle-Apples. These tree fruit are often despised due to how they cover the pavements and paths, but are tasty when cooked into Crackle-Apple Buckle. They can be found at [SPOILER]The Backwoods between the 15th and 20th of Fall [/SPOILER]
-- Chest-Nut. These crunchy tree nuts are harder to find and prepare than Hazelnuts, but are just as tasty when Roasted or cooked into a Chest-Nut & Cauliflower Soup. They can be found at [SPOILER]The Mountains between the 20th and 25th of Fall [/SPOILER]
--Rose-Pops. These bright red berries grow in more populated areas of the Valley, and are usually cooked into Rose-Pop Donuts. They can be found growing at [SPOILER]The BusStop and Town during the last few days of Fall and the first few days of Summer [/SPOILER]

--Fizzling Berry are sweet little orange berries hidden in brown shell-like leaves. They are commonly baked into an oozy Fizzling Cake. They can be found at [SPOILER] Ginger Island [/SPOILER]
[img]https://i.ibb.co/Gk5HVbq/03-Fruit-and-Nut-Dishes.png[/img]﻿﻿
-- On Thursdays Gus will sell a random recipe using the new Fruits and Nuts.

-- There have been rumours that if you put enough of certain forageable Fruits and Nuts into a seed-maker you can get a Sapling. I wonder if that's true? [SPOILER]Crackle-Apples has a Sapling and can be grown into a Tree. Chestnuts can be planted to grow a Chestnut Tree[/SPOILER]

-- All Berry-Bush fruits have compatibility and can be found in areas of Stardew Valley Expanded, Ridgeside Village, East Scarp and Cape Stardew. Have a look around for an extra chance to harvest these berries.


[b]**WILD FLOWERS OF FERNGILL*[/b]
The Fifth module of Forage of Ferngill. New wild flowers have been spotted popping up around the Valley and beyond.

[img]https://i.ibb.co/PFgs2Tw/Wild-Flowers.png[/img]
SPRING
-- Daye-Breaks (Common) -- These little white flowers sprout early in spring and can be seen covering whole fields. They can be found growing [SPOILER]all around the Valley[/SPOILER]
-- Blushing-Dawn (Rare) -- An early blooming vine flower. Looks like a rising sun. They can be found growing at [SPOILER]the Railway[/SPOILER]
-- Buttered-Bell (Very Rare) -- These hardy bell-shaped flowers are often found growing in the shade of tall buildings. They can be found growing [SPOILER]near the Community Centre[/SPOILER]

SUMMER
-- Luck-Puff (Common) -- These pink puffball flowers are said to make you lucky. They can be found growing [SPOILER]all around the Valley in Summer[/SPOILER]
-- Bright-Sides (Rare) -- A brilliant blue flower that has a sweet smell. They can be found growing at [SPOILER]Cindersap Forest[/SPOILER]
-- Lola Bloom (Very Rare) -- These bright white forest flowers are a common stop for Hummingbirds. They can be found growing around [SPOILER]the Mountain Lake[/SPOILER]

FALL
-- Buckle-Bray (Common) -- These tightly clustered purple flowers attract insects all throughout Fall. They can be found growing [SPOILER]around the Valley in Summer[/SPOILER]
-- Night Shadow (Rare) -- Highly poisonous to humans, but kept as an ornamental display. They can be found growing at [SPOILER]The Mountains[/SPOILER]
-- Bon-Bons (Very Rare) -- Coming in a range of colours, these are often seen filling forest clearings. They can be found growing near [SPOILER]Hat-Mouses shop[/SPOILER]

WINTER
-- Chill-Bell (Common) -- These flower are said to toll for the arrival of Winter. They can be found growing [SPOILER]all around the Valley[/SPOILER]

EXOTIC
-- Calico-Blaze -- These brilliant burning flowers bloom rarely in the Calico Desert.
-- Wish-Terra -- These cascading pink flowers are a vibrant sight at Ginger Island.

ADDON
The following flowers can also be found wild, and are also found in locations of the relevant Expansion mod
-- Shifter-Bloom (SVE) -- Hikers often catch flashes of these rare flowers in the forest.
-- Ridge-Riser (RSV) -- The drooping petals on this flower casts a deep shade below.
-- Fox-Shoes (ESC) -- Children's tales say that Foxes wear these as slippers to sneak around silently.

[img]https://i.ibb.co/KbG6KZN/Flower-Press.png[/img]

The Flower Press can be used to preserve any flower into a Pressed-Flower to increase its value. Unlocks at [SPOILER]Level 2 Foraging[/SPOILER]

[b]**KOMBUCHA OF FERNGILL**[/b]
The sixth and last module of Forage of Ferngill. This adds Kombucha to the game as a new Artisan Good. Kombucha is made by Mixing Scoby and Wild-Tea-Leaf in Kombucha Jars and letting it ferment for a few days. The result is a tasty tea that boots your Foraging. You can combine Plain Kombucha with other things in Kombucha Jars to make Flavoured Kombuchas. The flavours are

Floral -- Made by combining Plain Kombucha with [SPOILER] any Flower. This should work with any Modded flower too. [/SPOILER]
Nutty -- Made by combining Plain Kombucha with [SPOILER] Tree Seeds or Nuts. Acorns, Pine Cones, Maple Seeds work as do Chest-Nuts from Fruit and Nuts of Ferngill.  [/SPOILER]
Salty -- Made by combining Plain Kombucha with [SPOILER] Seaweed and both types of Algae work, as does Anisea-weed and Spysea-weed from Coastal Forage of Ferngill [/SPOILER]
Savoury -- Made by combining Plain Kombucha with [SPOILER] Mushrooms. Common Mushroom, Chanterelle, Morel and Truffle all work as do non-exotic mushrooms from Mushrooms of Ferngill. [/SPOILER]
Sour -- Made by combining Plain Kombucha with [SPOILER] Roots. Cave Carrot and Winter Root work as does Gaelic Root and Bardic Root from Roots of Ferngill [/SPOILER]
Sweet -- Made by combining Plain Kombucha with [SPOILER] any Fruit. This should work with any Modded fruit too. [/SPOILER]

[/SPOILER]
